report.source_text: We proceeded with three consecutive monthly 1ml-doses of triamcinolone acetonide injections (20mg/ml). The lesions gradually improved with no recurrence in the past 6 months.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old woman presented with a recurring lobulated warty lesion on her lower lip, which first appeared during her first pregnancy and reoccurred during her second. Initial histopathological examination revealed a dense predominantly plasmocytic infiltrate, epidermal thickening, and elongation of rete ridges, but no signs of neoplasia or malignancy. Further immunohistochemistry showed positivity for kappa, lambda, and CD138, confirming a polyclonal inflammatory reaction. Tests for fungal organisms, parasites, and Montenegro skin test were negative, and blood tests were normal. Based on these findings, plasmoacanthoma was diagnosed. The patient was treated with three consecutive monthly doses of triamcinolone acetonide injections, leading to gradual improvement of the lesions and no recurrence in 6 months.
